newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Spain's CASA opens pre-offset venture in Abu Dhabi.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CASA opens pre-offset venture in Abu Dhabi.

text.p: Spanish aerospace firm CASA (Construcciones Aeronauticas SA) on Monday opened an $8 million concrete brick and tile joint venture factory that could boost its chances of clinching an aircraft deal in Abu Dhabi.

State-owned CASA has a 49 percent stake in Giralda Emirates LLC factory, and its partner in the venture, al-Ain International, owns 51 percent, the company said in a statement given to reporters after the opening ceremony.
Al-Ain International is a group of United Arab Emirates investors.
The factory "is the pre-offset project of CASA in the context of a defence contract for which CASA is competing with a maritime patrol aircraft programme," it added without elaborating.
The oil-rich United Arab Emirates, which has emerged as a key customer in the international arms market, is seeking four such aircraft.
The UAE Offsets Group (UOG) was launched in July 1990 when the UAE activated a plan to buy high-tech weapons worth billions of dollars.

Defence companies are required to invest in projects with local investors in 49/51 joint ventures that generate added value to the UAE over a period of seven years equivalent to 60 percent of the added value of the sales contract under the offset programme.
The statement said CASA hoped the project, executed as a pre-commitment to UOG conditions, would boost its chances of clinching a multi-million dollar deal.
It supplied four transport planes to the UAE in 1982 for $20 million according to current market rates.
Eighty-percent of the raw materials used in the factory will be locally produced, the statement said.
It will have an annual capacity of one million square metres of high-quality bricks and tiles to help meet growing local demand for construction, the statement said.
CASA is the smallest of the four Airbus Industrie partners.
